conviction_note: Q3 is not pre-released beyond deliveries and the guide is the live line. My findings net slightly negative (-0.35): China is getting worse and Mercedes cut its outlook a week ago, against Q3 optics that should look flattered (the EUR 350m Aumovio settlement lands in Q3 and the severance charge most likely lands in Q4). So the scaled number is essentially a coin flip (p_up 51) on a 5% move. The two numbers differ in sign because the positives are one-offs this market sells, while the CFO's 'eher konservativ' and a +7% run-up make a second guidance cut less likely than the Mercedes read-across suggests. Both are partly priced, so the gap is small and I left it rather than forcing agreement.

already_public.what: FY2026 guidance cut by ad-hoc: Automotive EBIT margin 1-3% (was 4-6%), RoCE 1-5%, group EBT 'deutlicher Rueckgang', Automotive FCF > EUR 2.5bn, buyback unchanged

H1 2026: Q2 Automotive EBIT EUR 629m, margin 2.3% (tariffs -1.25pp, BBA PPA -1.2pp), H1 margin 3.6%, H1 FCF EUR 1.3bn. FY guide confirmed and stated to include 'bis zu 1,25 Prozentpunkten' from the personnel restructuring programme
Aumovio pays BMW EUR 350m to settle the IBS brake warranty dispute, in two instalments in Q3 and Q4 2026 (counterparty ad-hoc)
Capital Market Day: 2028 Automotive EBIT margin corridor of 3-5% as an interim step, 8-10% at the start of the next decade; further changes in spring 2027

new_in_release.expect: Q3 Automotive EBIT margin, probably around or above the top of the 1-3% corridor thanks to the Aumovio settlement, which RBC says could take it above the range. Underlying margin is likely weaker than Q2 given China -24.8%. Mildly positive optics, and the market will strip out the one-off.

Most likely the 1-3% corridor is confirmed, possibly narrowed. Mercedes cut on 2026-10-27 citing China and Q4 costs, so a narrowing toward the lower half is a real risk. A cut is less likely given the CFO's 'eher konservativ' on 2026-10-14. Direction unknown, skewed slightly negative.
Q3 Automotive FCF. H1 was EUR 1.3bn against a > EUR 2.5bn guide, and RBC flags working-capital pressure in Q3. The first Aumovio instalment helps. Slight negative risk.
When the personnel restructuring charge is booked and how much it is. Agreements are due by mid-November, so most likely Q4. An update on the cost could move the FY corridor position.
The EUR 625m buyback tranche ends by end-November. A new programme is not expected before spring 2027.

bar: Q3 group revenue about EUR 29.9bn and group EBIT about EUR 1.7bn. Two secondary sources agree: J.P. Morgan EUR 29.7bn / EUR 1.68bn (https://admiralmarkets.com/education/articles/shares/bmw-shares-profit-warning-2026, 2026-10-16) and a 'Konsens' of EUR 29.9bn / EUR 1.7bn (https://www.boerse-express.com/news/articles/bmw-aktie-quartalszahlen-am-4-november-2026-956578, as summarised in search). The FY Automotive margin bar is the company's own 1-3% guide, with consensus about 2%. I could not source a Q3 Automotive EBIT margin consensus, so sizes on the Q3 margin line are capped small.
session_check: bmo: BMW IR says the Quarterly Statement to 30 September 2026 is 'Download available on 04 November 2026' (https://www.bmwgroup.com/en/investor-relations/company-reports.html). The conference-call page lists speeches at 08:30 CET, journalists' Q&A at 09:05 and analysts' Q&A at 10:15 (https://www.bmwgroup.com/de/investor-relations/telefonkonferenzen-quartalsmitteilungen.html). Release reported for 07:30 (https://www.boerse-express.com/news/articles/bmw-aktie-quartalszahlen-am-4-november-2026-956578).
positioning_check: Bundesanzeiger net short 2.61% across 5 disclosed sellers, position date 2026-10-27, unchanged from the previous cache (0.0pp change), so neither building nor covering. Moderate, not crowded. Source: baseline positioning block (https://www.bundesanzeiger.de/pub/en/nlp?0--top~csv~form~panel-form-csv~resource~link, as of 2026-11-02).

findings.finding: Aumovio's ad-hoc commits it to pay BMW EUR 350m in two instalments in Q3 and Q4 2026. RBC expects this to lift BMW's Q3 Automotive EBIT margin above the 1-3% corridor, so Q3 reported optics should look strong but non-recurring.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No BMW-specific record of a one-off-driven beat. On a European name (H&M) a beat made of a one-off was sold. BMW's Q2 print matched the margin consensus exactly and the stock moved -0.2%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced. RBC flagged it publicly and analysts normalise it away. What stays unpriced is only how BMW classifies it: if it sits inside Automotive EBIT and BMW does not call it out, the headline margin prints above models that assumed it would be excluded. If it were fully priced, the consensus EBIT of about EUR 1.7bn would already sit well above Q2's EUR 1.63bn, which it only modestly does.

findings.finding: BMW closed its German voluntary severance programme early because the target was reached sooner than planned, and applicants hear by mid-November whether they get an agreement. So the roughly EUR 1bn restructuring charge most likely books in Q4, not Q3 (RBC also expects the larger hit in Q4), which leaves Q3 clean and brings the savings forward.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The July 2026 job-cut announcement ('BMW baut weltweit 8000 Jobs ab - Aktie unbeeindruckt') did not move the stock.
findings.original_quote: BMW closed its voluntary severance program in Germany early ... target was reached sooner than planned (German article as summarised by WebFetch; the German original sentence was not returned verbatim). From the 2026-10-16 report: 'Das Abfindungsprogramm selbst wird auf eine dreistellige Millionensumme geschaetzt' (the severance programme itself is estimated at a three-digit million sum).
findings.why_not_priced: Early closure was reported only in German regional and finance press, and the release is the first place BMW states the charge and its timing. If the market had priced faster savings, consensus FY2027 margins would have moved after mid-October, and I found no such revision. Uncertainty: if BMW books an IAS 37 provision in Q3, reported Q3 takes the hit instead, though analysts would adjust for it.
findings.independence: https://www.cash-online.de/a/bmw-bremst-abfindungsprogramm-wegen-ansturm-der-belegschaft-727773/ (2026-10-16, programme paused on overwhelming demand); RBC Q4 timing via https://finimize.com/content/bmws-q3-margins-could-beat-its-2026-target-says-rbc

findings.finding: In an interview on 2026-10-14, CFO Walter Mertl called the company's current planning conservative ('Unsere aktuelle Planung ist eher konservativ') and said overpromising would be wrong. This lowers the odds of a second cut to the FY corridor in the Q3 release.
findings.original_quote: Unsere aktuelle Planung ist eher konservativ. Das kann man zum Beispiel daran erkennen, dass wir für 2028 eine Ebit-Marge von 3 bis 5% in Aussicht stellen. Zu viel zu versprechen wäre falsch. (Our current planning is rather conservative. You can see that, for example, in our 3-5% EBIT margin target for 2028. Promising too much would be wrong.)
findings.why_not_priced: The interview is paywalled, in German, and the example he gives is 2028, not 2026. It reads as a statement about the planning stance, not a number. If priced, BMW would not have dipped 1.8% on the Mercedes cut; it did, then recovered.

findings.finding: Peer read-across: on 2026-10-27, with its Q3 numbers, Mercedes-Benz cut its 2026 cars margin guide to 2-3% (from 3-5%), citing China and higher Q4 costs including material costs. Its Q3 adjusted cars margin was 2.5%, and the stock fell 3.9% while BMW fell 1.8% the same day. BMW carries the same China exposure and fully consolidates BBA.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: BMW -1.77% on 2026-10-27, then recovered to a new local high by 2026-11-02 (+1.83%). In June, BMW's own cut dragged Mercedes down 3-4%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: BMW lost 1.8% that day and has since regained it, so the market reads Mercedes as company-specific. If the market expected BMW to follow with a cut or a low-end narrowing, BMW would not sit at a one-month high going into the print. The Q4 material-cost driver Mercedes named has not been addressed by BMW. This is a peer proxy, not a BMW document.

findings.finding: BMW's China deliveries fell 24.8% in Q3, faster than the 20.4% H1 decline, while Q2 already showed a EUR 1.8bn volume/mix/pricing hit 'mainly China'. Q3 underlying Automotive margin before one-offs is therefore at risk of falling below Q2's 2.3%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 had a similar China-driven decline. The margin matched consensus and the stock moved -0.2% on the day and -1.5% the next.
findings.original_quote: China-region -24.8% to 114,355 units; H1: 'Im ersten Halbjahr lagen die Auslieferungen in China um 20,4 Prozent unter dem Vorjahresniveau' (H1 deliveries in China were 20.4% below the prior year; from the H1 CFO speech)
findings.why_not_priced: The volume line was pre-released on 2026-10-13 and is priced. What is not public is the China pricing and mix effect, which BBA full consolidation passes straight into Automotive EBIT. Sized near zero for that reason.
findings.independence: https://www.press.bmwgroup.com/austria/article/detail/T0459757DE (2026-07-30, H1 China -20.4% and the EUR 1.8bn Q2 volume/mix/pricing hit)

findings.finding: In October 2026 BMW cancelled shifts at short notice at Regensburg, its highest-volume European plant, citing short-term external parts-supply bottlenecks. This is a Q4 production and volume risk that could feed into the FY guide commentary.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured reaction. The stock rose through the second half of October.
findings.source_date: 2026-10 (after 2026-10-14, per the page's reference to the RBC target cut as earlier)
findings.original_quote: Das Unternehmen führte die Unterbrechungen auf kurzfristige Engpässe bei der externen Teileversorgung zurück. (The company attributed the interruptions to short-term bottlenecks in external parts supply; quoted in https://www.boerse-express.com/news/articles/bmw-aktie-quartalszahlen-am-4-november-2026-956578)
findings.why_not_priced: It was reported only in German finance and regional sites, with no BMW quantification. If the market expected a material volume hit, the stock would not have risen about 7% over 20 sessions. It is small and unquantified.

findings.finding: Automotive FCF stood at EUR 1.3bn after H1 against a > EUR 2.5bn FY guide. Q2 working capital took EUR 1.3bn out, and RBC flags working-capital pressure on Q3 cash. FCF is the line that can undercut a margin-flattered quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No BMW-specific record. On a European name (Luceco) negative FCF outweighed a raised guide (-5.5%).
findings.original_quote: Nach sechs Monaten belief sich der Free Cashflow auf 1,3 Milliarden Euro. Für das Gesamtjahr strebt die BMW Group unverändert einen Free Cashflow im Segment Automobile von über 2,5 Milliarden Euro an. (After six months free cash flow was EUR 1.3bn. For the full year BMW Group still targets Automotive free cash flow of more than EUR 2.5bn.)
findings.why_not_priced: The H1 number is public. What is unknown is whether Q3 working capital consumed cash. The first Aumovio instalment (part of EUR 350m) partly offsets it. If the market feared an FCF guide cut, it would show in a weaker share price than the one-month high it trades at.

outside_window.finding: Severance applicants learn by mid-November whether they get a termination agreement. The final size of the restructuring charge and its Q4 booking resolve after the window, unless BMW quantifies them on 2026-11-04.
Further strategic changes and 2027 guidance are flagged for spring 2027 ('Weitere Änderungen im Frühjahr 2027').

baseline_tension: Mostly agrees with the baseline. The +7.25% 20-day run-up and flat 2.61% short (lean +1.2) price a relief print with the guide confirmed. My findings net slightly negative on China and the Mercedes read-across, but those are partly priced, so I do not lean against the lean.
language_note: German press (cash-online, boerse-express) carried that the severance programme closed early with its target reached and that agreements are due by mid-November, which sets the Q3/Q4 timing of the restructuring charge. English sources carried only RBC's 'bigger hit in Q4'.
The CFO's 'Unsere aktuelle Planung ist eher konservativ' (Börsen-Zeitung, 2026-10-14) appeared only in German.
The Regensburg shift cancellations for parts shortages appeared only in German regional and finance press.
The H1 CFO speech in German gave the Personalstrukturprogramm as included in the 1-3% guide ('bis zu 1,25 Prozentpunkten'). The English summaries I found did not state that inclusion.
lessons_applied: 'A beat made of a one-off is sold' (H&M): Aumovio settlement finding cut from +0.3 to +0.1; p_up 52 -> 51.

'You were right about the number and too small about the move' and 'the move is in the guide': abs_move_pct raised from 4.0 to 5.0, because the quarter is not pre-released and a corridor narrowing is plausible after Mercedes' cut (BMW's own confirmed-guide prints moved +5.4% and +6.9%).
'A finding about a number the market has already been told is worth 0': China/deliveries finding cut from -0.3 to -0.15 (volume pre-released 2026-10-13).
'A narrow proxy loses ... macro-to-company transmission is a hypothesis': Mercedes read-across cut from -0.6 to -0.4; Regensburg parts shortage (unquantified) cut from -0.2 to -0.1.
'Cash can outweigh a raised guide' (Luceco): FCF finding raised in weight from -0.2 to -0.3.
